page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, consisting of 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. A key hardware feature is the inclusion of 402 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the average tier. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks show limitations. Multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores fall into the weak category. Memory bandwidth tests, including both small and large block read/write operations, also register in the lower performance tier, alongside a poor rating for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Despite memory bandwidth constraints, the processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptography. These features assist in workloads like static web serving, which achieved an average throughput of 6.5 GB/sec, and light text processing. The instance is suited for general-purpose applications, basic web serving, and workloads that benefit from fast local NVMe storage but do not demand high multi-core scaling or intensive memory bandwidth.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM and 402 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between average single-core capabilities and weaker multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests, perform in the average tier, whereas multi-core stress tests and database operations fall into the lower performance brackets. With its bundled high-speed local storage and moderate single-core throughput, this instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and applications requiring fast local scratch space rather than heavy multi-threaded computation.
